title: Denominator from a linear recurrence
statement:
Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $C(T)=\sum_{n\geq0}c_nT^n\in K[[T]]$ a formal power series [def-weil-formal-power-series]. Let $m\geq0$, $d\geq1$ be integers and $a_0,\ldots,a_{d-1}\in K$ such that $(c_n)$ satisfies the linear recurrence of order $d$ with coefficients $a_0,\ldots,a_{d-1}$ from the index $m$ on [def-weil-eventual-linear-recurrence]: $c_{n+d}+a_{d-1}c_{n+d-1}+\cdots+a_0c_n=0$ for $n\geq m$. Put
$$
Q(T)=1+a_{d-1}T+a_{d-2}T^2+\cdots+a_0T^d\in K[T]
$$
[def-weil-polynomial-ring], so $[T^0]Q=1$ and $[T^j]Q=a_{d-j}$ for $1\leq j\leq d$ [def-weil-polynomial-coefficient]. Then $Q(0)=1$, and the product $QC\in K[[T]]$ (with $Q$ regarded as a power series [def-weil-polynomial-as-power-series]) is a polynomial $P\in K[T]$ with $[T^N]P=0$ for every $N\geq m+d$; explicitly $[T^N]P=c_N+\sum_{j=1}^{\min(N,d)}a_{d-j}c_{N-j}$ for $0\leq N<m+d$.

source.place: Ch. II, §27, proof of Lemma 27.9, p. 157 (quoting Bourbaki, Algèbre, IV.5, Exercise 3(a): f lies in k(t) iff its coefficients satisfy a linear relation λ_1a_n+…+λ_ra_{n+r-1}=0 for all n≥d; stated, not proved); the direction 'recurrence implies rational'
